source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: At the FreshMart checkout by the produce aisle, a shopper with barely three items waited watching the belt, toward the bagging counter, out of the scanner's glow, so she had eyed a stranger behind her. The line stretched on. This queue during rush is jammed against eight because a divider slides slowly along it. She nudged it as she claimed her sliver of space that nobody was defending anyhow. The narrow bar is monitored to remain fair. Impatiently he sighed, a rushed breath, and I caught it up beneath me. Three carts back, restlessly they crowded us toward the aisle Register Six against a wall by the Loyalty Kiosk. It was during the beeping that a cashier had announced a total to bill the flustered customer bagging beneath his hand. She scanned it too, past the reader and quickly.
